direct_answer:
Aker BP states that its double materiality assessment (DMA) is a systematic, four-step process that maps impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs), their dependencies, and their connection to Aker BP’s own operations and value chain, considering activities, business relationships and geographies. It covers both (i) impact materiality (inside-out: impacts on environment and society) and (ii) financial materiality (outside-in: financial risks/opportunities to the business model and performance, including reputational risk and dependencies on natural, human and social resources). IROs are assessed using severity × likelihood (aligned with the company’s enterprise risk management scales and documented in the same tool as other company risks), with special attention to dependencies between impacts and corresponding risks/opportunities. Stakeholder dialogue is described as supporting identification of risks, opportunities and actual/potential impacts, and the company notes it will update the DMA as new information becomes available. The resulting material IROs form the basis for the report and were reviewed by the Board of Directors, Audit & Risk Committee and Executive Management Team. [Source 8][Source 10][Source 4][Source 1]

From both an impact and a financial perspective, Aker BP identifies as highest-priority (high impact and high financial relevance) the following sustainability matters: climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, and resource use and circular economy. [Source 4]

Other matters are also considered material (with significant impacts and compliance relevance but comparatively lower financial materiality): affected communities, biodiversity and ecosystems, and workers in the value chain. Water and marine resources are assessed as having lower overall materiality relative to other topics (though Aker BP notes water consumption may be material in parts of its upstream value chain due to increased construction activity abroad). [Source 4][Source 1]
compliance_rationale: The passages evidence that Aker BP performed a DMA covering both impact and financial materiality, describes key methodological elements (four-step process; severity×likelihood; value chain coverage; consideration of dependencies; inclusion of reputational risk and resource dependencies; stakeholder dialogue; governance review of outputs) and discloses a set of material topics including those material from both perspectives. [Source 10][Source 4][Source 8][Source 1] However, the retrieved excerpts do not provide the full four-step description (Figure 9), explicit thresholds/criteria used to determine materiality, nor a complete list of material IROs (Table 3 is referenced but not included), limiting full ESRS 1 substantiation from the provided evidence. [Source 1][Source 4][Source 10]
disclosure_gaps: Full description of the four-step DMA process (Figure 9) and how each step was executed is not included in the retrieved passages. [Source 8][Source 10]
Explicit qualitative/quantitative thresholds or criteria used to conclude materiality for impacts and for financial effects are not provided in the retrieved passages. [Source 10]
Complete output of the DMA (the full list of material IROs in Table 3) is referenced but not provided in the retrieved passages. [Source 1]

Clear mapping of each identified material sustainability matter to whether it is impact-material, financially material, or both (beyond the high-level matrix narrative) is not fully shown in the retrieved passages. [Source 4][Source 10]
Details on how affected stakeholders were engaged specifically within the DMA (who, when, and how inputs changed outcomes) are not evidenced beyond general statements. [Source 4][Source 10]
More explicit linkage between due diligence outcomes and the DMA results is not shown beyond cross-references and general due diligence descriptions. [Source 3][Source 9]
key_findings: DMA revised in 2024 based on new information, implementation guidance and EFRAG draft oil & gas sector standard; includes mapping of IROs, dependencies and value-chain connection. [Source 8]

DMA covers inside-out impacts and outside-in financial risks/opportunities, including reputational risk and dependencies on natural, human and social resources; considers interdependencies between impacts and risks/opportunities. [Source 10]
IROs assessed using severity × likelihood, aligned with enterprise risk management scales and documented in the same tool as other company risks. [Source 10][Source 8]
Highest-priority topics (high impact and high financial relevance): climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, resource use and circular economy. [Source 4]
Also material (lower financial materiality): affected communities, biodiversity and ecosystems, workers in the value chain. [Source 4]

Water and marine resources assessed as lower overall materiality, but water consumption may be material in parts of the upstream value chain due to increased construction activity abroad. [Source 4][Source 1]
Material IROs form the basis for the report and were reviewed by the Board, Audit & Risk Committee and Executive Management Team. [Source 1]
